\chapter{Preface}
This book collects a series of research manuscripts on a metaplectic
Jacquet--Langlands transfer between the $n$-fold cover of the
multiplicative group of a central division algebra $D$ of prime degree
$r$ over a number field and the Kazhdan--Patterson cover of
$\mathrm{GL}(r)$.  It is ongoing research: the text distinguishes
complete proofs, results established in the literature or in other
chapters, conditional statements and open problems by the labels of
\S\ref{gl:labels}, and \textbf{the full metaplectic Jacquet--Langlands
correspondence is not claimed}.

\paragraph{Sources.}  Chapters~\ref{ch:I}--\ref{ch:W} are the
following manuscripts, written in November 2026 and frozen when this
book was assembled; their drafts, revision logs and referee reports
remain in the project repository
(\texttt{github.com/wdjoyner/metaplectic-jl}).
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll@{}}\toprule
Chapter & Source & Authors (as on the source)\\\midrule
\ref{ch:I} & Part~I, Draft~11 & Joyner, Claude, ChatGPT\\
\ref{ch:II} & Part~II, Draft~10 & Joyner, Claude, ChatGPT\\
\ref{ch:III} & Part~III, Draft~10 & Joyner, ChatGPT, Claude\\
\ref{ch:IV} & Part~IV, concluding Draft~6 & Joyner, ChatGPT, Claude\\
\ref{ch:W} & Companion paper on the rank-two wild place, Draft~8 & Joyner, ChatGPT, Claude\\
\bottomrule\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Chapter~\ref{ch:lit} gathers the literature review of Part~I and the
related-work sections of the other manuscripts; Chapter~\ref{ch:notation}
gathers the shared glossary of the series and the notation sections of
the manuscripts; Chapter~\ref{ch:summary} gathers their summaries of
results; and the Appendix holds the tables and verification scripts of
Chapter~\ref{ch:W}.

\paragraph{What changed in the conversion.}  No statement, proof,
hypothesis or status label was changed.  References between the
manuscripts, which were typed by hand (``Part~I, Lemma~2.2''), are now
cross-references to the numbering of this book; references to the
literature are now citations to one bibliography; the macros of each
manuscript are kept, local to its chapter.  The source drafts sometimes
cite other Parts by an older numbering; each such reference was mapped
through the numbering of the draft it was written against.  Where a
manuscript names an item with the wrong type (for example
``Definition'' for what is a lemma), the reference now shows the
item's actual type; these cases are listed in the revision log.  Each
chapter still has its own introduction, which repeats some of the
setting; removing that repetition is left for a later draft.

\paragraph{Contributions.}  The acknowledgments of the manuscripts are
reproduced below.  ChatGPT (OpenAI) and Claude (Anthropic) drafted and
refereed parts of the series; the referee reports and the responses to
them are in the repository.  Independent human review is the next step,
and the mathematical claims should be assessed independently.

\chapter{Introduction}\label{ch:intro}
\section{The setting}
Let $K$ be a totally imaginary number field containing the group
$\mu_n$ of $n$-th roots of unity, with $n$ odd; let $r$ be a prime with
$(n,r)=1$; and let $D$ be a central division algebra of dimension $r^2$
over $K$, ramified at the finite set $S$ of places, containing a cyclic
maximal subfield $L$.  The book compares two $n$-fold covers: the cover
of $D^\times_{\mathbb A}$ from the author's corrected 1988 paper on the
metaplectic analog of Kazhdan's ``endoscopic'' lifting \cite{JC}, and
the Kazhdan--Patterson cover of $\mathrm{GL}(r,\mathbb A_K)$ with twisting
parameter $c_v$, where $n\mid r-1+2rc_v$.  Both are subgroups of one
cover of $\mathrm{GL}(r,\mathbb A_L)$ (\cref{I:prop:restriction}).  The
approach follows the trace-formula proof of the classical
Jacquet--Langlands correspondence and uses the metaplectic
correspondence of Flicker and Kazhdan \cite{FK} with the corrections of
Zou \cite{Z}.  The global data and conventions are fixed in
\S\S\ref{gl:global}--\ref{gl:cocycle}.

\section{The chapters}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item Chapter~\ref{ch:lit} reviews the literature, and
Chapter~\ref{ch:notation} collects the notation, the status labels and
the cocycle normalization.
\item Chapter~\ref{ch:I} constructs the two covers inside one ambient
cover, identifies their covered elliptic tori on good elements
(Theorem~A), proves matching of test functions supported on the regular
set (Theorem~B), and proves a global transfer under a non-cancellation
hypothesis (Theorem~C).
\item Chapter~\ref{ch:II} proves matching of arbitrary genuine test
functions (Theorems~D and~E) and an improved global transfer
(Theorem~C$'$).
\item Chapter~\ref{ch:III} studies the division-algebra side through a
unitary transform $L_D$ of class functions, proves that it carries
irreducible characters to irreducible genuine characters at places not
dividing $n$, obtains the character relation there in the range of the
corrected Flicker--Kazhdan correspondence, and gives the obstruction at
places dividing $n$.
\item Chapter~\ref{ch:IV} reconciles the cocycle conventions, studies
power maps and good elements for every maximal torus, proves a toral
positivity criterion at places dividing $n$, and proves a conditional
global comparison.
\item Chapter~\ref{ch:W} treats the wild place of the running example
in degree two: the transform of the trivial character, and of every
representation trivial on the third congruence subgroup, is a genuine
irreducible character.
\item Chapter~\ref{ch:summary} lists the results of
Chapters~\ref{ch:I}--\ref{ch:W} with their labels.
\end{itemize}

\section{The running example}
Every chapter tests its constructions on one case: $K=\mathbb Q(\zeta_3)$,
$n=3$, $r=2$, and the quaternion algebra $D=(-1,4-\zeta_3)_K$, ramified
exactly at the prime above $3$ (a wild place, where $b_D=3$ and
$c_D=27$) and at one prime above $7$ (a tame place).  Each chapter has a
short subsection on it, and the note
\texttt{notes/mjl\_running\_example.tex} in the repository works it out
across the chapters.

\section{Main open problems}
Integrality of $L_D$ at places dividing $n$ in general; the full global
comparison of the cover of $D^\times$ with the cover of $\mathrm{GL}(r)$,
which needs matching at the places where $D$ splits and at the complex
places; and the removal of the auxiliary support and packet hypotheses
of Chapters~\ref{ch:I}--\ref{ch:II}.  Chapter~\ref{ch:W},
\S\ref{W:sec:future}, discusses what a general wild result would need.
